The Beatles?

Not me man. I saw Dylan & Petty on that tour and it was *great*. Bob is always as good as who is backing him up and the Heartbreakers, super tight road dogs that they were, gave him a recognizable tight and tough sound. It jumped.

Ive seen Dylan many many times over the years in various incarnations going back to that great 10 night stand at the Warfield in SF for the Slow Train Coming tour - with diminishing returns I have to admit - and that Petty gig is right there for me for favorites.

Certainly over the last ...10 years for sure..Bob has come across as downright miserable. Just: "What are we even doin' here man?" Makes Van Morrison, a noted curmudgeon at best, seem as gregarious as Dave Grohl.

I will say for sure: whenever you write off Dylan he comes along with one of the greatest songs he ever wrote ( see : Mississippi) *and* I never saw a Dylan concert where I didn't want to go right back in and watch the show I just saw. Even if is because I didn't recognize what he was playing until it was half over : /

Frankly, Im discouraged to see what the results would bring. The real reality of it would probably crush my humanity forever. Lord knows I don't need to be *more* cynical.
